uab: mab (mab) — son; noun m., soft-mutated after a personal name in a patronymic (Guawl uab Clut 'Gwawl son of Clud') · also soft after predicative yn (yn uab y wr arall 'a son of another man'; yn uab y Pwyll 'a son of Pwyll') · also soft in apposition to a noun (uy nei, uab uy chwaer 'my nephew, son of my sister') and in address (Oy a uab Duw 'O son of God')
oed: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. imperfect 'was' (Pwyll... a oed yn arglwyd) · also oed 'appointed time, tryst', noun m., = oet (gwna oed a mi 'make an appointment with me')
arglwyd: arglwyd (arglwydd) — lord; noun m., term of address
ar: ar — (1) preposition 'on, upon; at' (ar Hafgan; ar y carw; ar y gilyd 'against the other'); (2) the article yr after a vowel, 'that which' (noc ar a uu 'than what was'; Ar ny del 'and whoever does not come') · also (3) 'with, accompanied by' (ar y ganuet marchauc 'with his hundred horsemen'); 'in' (ar y ssynnwyr e hun 'in his own senses'; ar perued y digrifwch 'in the middle of the merriment'); ar neill law Pwyll 'on one side of Pwyll'; ar uyrr 'quickly'; ar hynny 'thereupon' (see yny) · also 'over' (ar yr ynys hon 'over this island'); 'after the manner of' (ar ureint kyweirdeb 'in the manner of the arrangement'); 'on' a decision (disgynnu ar gymryt hynny 'settled on taking that'); 'ar ol' 'after' (ar ol Matholwch 'after Matholwch'); ar dec 'on ten' (see dec) · also 'concerning, about', where am would be expected (ac ar Yspydaut Benn 'and concerning the Hospitality of the Head'; the Red Book also ar) · ar + verbal noun, 'to, in order to' (doethwyf i ar diuetha y pryf 'I have come to destroy the creature')
a: a — (1) preverbal/relative particle before a verb, causes soft mutation (Pwyll … a oed; ef a welei); (2) 'and' before a consonant, spirant mutation (a chanu, a fob); (3) 'with' (a'y gydymdeithon; gyt a thi); (4) vocative particle (A unben); (5) 'whoever, what' before a verb (a del 'whoever may come'; a wnaethost 'what you did') · (6) 3 sg. present of mynet 'goes' (nat a odyno 'that he does not go from there'; yd a hitheu 'she goes'); (7) interrogative particle before a verb (a oes …? 'is there …?'; a dywedy di …? 'will you tell …?'); (8) in a'y kymriw neu archolleu the editorial a'y stands for the conjunction ae 'either' (ae … neu 'either … or'; the Red Book has ae kymriw ae archolleu): read the two halves together as ae · (9) 'as' after an equative (kyn debycket a'r mab 'as like as the boy'; kyn ureisket oed a mab chweblwyd 'as stout as a boy of six') · also 'to, towards' with spirant mutation (parth a Hardlech 'towards Harlech'; y tu a Chernyw 'the side towards Cornwall') · also (10) linking a fronted adjective to its noun, with soft mutation of the noun (ys drwc a gedymdeith 'a bad companion'); here a is not the conjunction
pryderi: Pryderi (Pryderi) — proper name, the son of Pwyll and Rhiannon, named from pryder 'care'; no mutation
pwyll: Pwyll — proper name, the tale's protagonist; means 'sense, discretion' (pwyll)
un: un (un) — one; numeral/adjective (un dyrnaut 'one blow') · also 'same' (yn un ansawd 'in the same appearance'; yr un ford 'the same way') and the pronoun 'one (of them)' (Un a gyuodes 'one rose')
cantref: cantref (cantref) — a 'hundred townships', the main administrative division of medieval Wales; noun m. (seith cantref Dyuet 'the seven cantrefs of Dyfed')
ugeint: ugeint (ugain) — twenty; numeral m. (ar ugeint 'on twenty' = 'and twenty'); no mutation
yn: yn — (1) 'in' (yn Arberth; nasal mutation: yn nyblyc); (2) predicative 'as' with soft mutation (yn wisc hela, yn arglwyd); (3) with a verbal noun, progressive (yn dyuot 'coming'); (4) before an adjective, adverbial (yn llawen 'gladly') · (5) yn yd 'to where' (ymchwelut yn yd oed Pwyll 'returning to where Pwyll was') · also yn yd 'as, while, when' (Ac yn yd aeth pawb ym pen yr arueu 'and while all went to arms'; the sense uncertain) · also 'our', a spelling of an (ein), with no mutation (yn anniuer ninheu 'our own company'; yn ymborth 'our sustenance'; yn diuetha 'our destroying') · also 'into' with rithyaw (eu rithyaw yn llygot 'to change them into mice')
y: y — (1) the article 'the' (y llys); (2) 'his, her, its' (y uryt: soft mutation = his; y hymdidan: h-prefix = her); (3) 'to' (y hela, y gyuoeth); (4) preverbal particle after a fronted adverb or object (yno y bu, Pwyll... a oed); (5) the relative in oblique relations (o'r a welsei) · (6) 'from' in y gan, y wrth 'from, compared with' (y gan y uarch 'from his horse'; y wrth y ffryt hi 'compared with her form'); (7) infixed object 'him, her, it' after a (a'y guelei 'who saw her'); (8) in a'y kymriw it is the second letter of ae 'either' (see a) · also (9) y am, y amdanaw 'from about, off' (y amdanaw 'off him'); y am hynny 'around that, beyond that, besides' · also (10) 'their' (for eu), with no mutation (y bot 'their being'; y kymryt 'their taking' = to take them) · also (11) 'in' (y'th wlat ti 'in your country') · (12) the particle y before mae introducing a reported fact (y may brawt … a wnaeth hynny 'that it is a brother who did that') · also (13) for predicative yn 'as', with soft mutation (Mi a rodaf Duw y uach it 'I give God as surety to you'; the Red Book yn vach) · (14) y ar 'from off' (y ar seith cantref Dyuet 'from off the seven cantrefs of Dyfed') · also y 'its, his' before a verbal noun, standing for the noun's object and softening it (na'y werthu 'nor selling it'; na'y ollwng 'nor releasing it')
deheu: deheu (de) — south, the right (hand); noun m. (o deheu Iwerdon 'from the south of Ireland'); after o 'from' the soft mutation (d>dd) is not shown, d serving for both
sef: sef (sef) — it is (this), that is; presentative particle introducing an explanation or answer
rei: rei (rhai) — some, some people; pronoun (rei o'r maes hwnn 'some of this field')
hynny: hynny — 'that (thing)'; demonstrative pronoun, very frequent (a hynny 'and that')
dyuet: Dyuet (Dyfed) — proper name, the region of south-west Wales
phedwar: pedwar (pedwar) — four; numeral (a phedwar cantref Keredigyawn 'and four cantrefs of Ceredigion'); spirant-mutated (p>ph) after a 'and'
ystrat: ystrat (ystrad) — vale, valley floor; noun m., in the name Ystrat Tywi 'the vale of the Tywi'; no mutation
tywi: Tywi (Tywi) — proper name, the river Tywi (Ystrat Tywi 'the vale of Tywi'); no mutation
ac: a — 'and' before a vowel (ac ef); also the preposition a 'with' before a vowel (ymgael ac ef 'meet with him', ymordiwes ac ef) · the manuscript also writes ac before some consonants (Ac wal, Ac val, ac racdaw) · also 'as' after an equative or kymeint (kymeint ac ynot ti 'as much as in you'; mor anwedus ac ar y wnaethoed 'as unseemly as what she had done')
yr: yr — (1) the article 'the' before a vowel (yr erchwys); (2) 'for, for the sake of' preposition (yr Duw 'for God's sake', yr guaret gormes 'for removing the oppression') · (3) 'for all, however' before an equative-type noun and a clause (yr araued y kerdei y uarch 'for all the slowness with which his horse went'); (4) in yr meityn 'for a while (since)'; (5) the verbal particle y, yd, written yr before a vowel (yr ymordiwedei a hi 'that he would overtake her') · also (6) the perfective particle ry written yr, softening the verb (yr gyscwys 'has slept'); the article before an independent possessive (yr eidunt 'theirs'); 'for' with an abstract noun (yr bychanet 'for the smallness') · also the article before hwnn, honn, 'the one' (yr hwnn y tu a Chernyw 'the one on the side towards Cornwall'; yr honn a uu tryded anuat paluawt 'the one that was the third unfortunate blow') · also yr (er) 'for all' before the relative a (yr a welsynt o ouut 'for all the grief they had seen') · also the article before a consonant in kyrchu yr gaer 'making for the fort' (read as the article, as the second witness takes it) · yr pan 'since' (yr pan welsei ef 'since he had seen'); the verb after it is soft-mutated
oes: bot (bod) — to be; present 3 sg. existential 'there is' (Nit oes yndi nep)
ny: ny (ni/nid) — negative particle 'not', base form before a consonant with soft mutation · also spirant mutation of c, p, t (ny chewch 'you will not get'; ny thygyawd 'it did not avail'); soft mutation of g (ny wybydei 'knew not')
bydei: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. habitual imperfect 'would be' (modern byddai) (na bydei launach no chynt 'it would not be fuller than before'); b is not changed after na
uyw: byw (byw) — alive, living; adjective, soft-mutated (b>u) after predicative yn (yn uyw gyd ac wynt 'alive with them')
namyn: namyn (namyn) — except, but; conjunction (namyn ti 'but you')
tra: tra (tra) — while; conjunction (tra deweis wrthyt ti 'while I kept silent') · also (2) 'very', before an adjective with spirant mutation (tra chyuoethauc 'very mighty'); (3) 'while' with the verb sometimes soft-mutated (tra barhaud) · also 'beyond', preposition (tra y gefyn 'beyond his back', i.e. back again)
uei: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. imperfect subjunctive 'might be', soft-mutated after a (a uei uwy no hynny) · also soft-mutated after ban 'when' (ban uei uwyaf 'when it was most') · also soft after yny 'until' (yny uei agos y guyr idaw 'until the men would be near it')
deudroet: deudroed (deudroed) — two feet; deu 'two' + troed, the t softened (d) after deu (a'y deudroet 'with his two feet'); modern deudroed
morwyn: morwyn (morwyn) — maiden, girl; noun f. (teccaf morwyn 'the fairest maiden'; morwyn gystal 'so good a maiden'); no mutation (radical)
onyt: onyt (onid) — unless; conjunction (onyt ti a'm gwrthyt 'unless (it be) you (who) reject me') · also 'except, but' (un dyn yma onyt pedwar dyn 'one man here except four men')
uorwyn: morwyn (morwyn) — maiden; noun f., soft-mutated in address (A uorwyn 'O maiden'), after the article (y uorwyn 'the maiden') and after o (o uorwyn 'of maiden') · also soft after am 'about' (am uorwyn kystal 'about a maiden so good')
gyt: kyt (cyd) — together; in y gyt (a) 'together (with)' (y gyt ac wynt 'together with them')
ef: ef (ef) — 'he, him'; independent 3 sg. m. pronoun
uerch: merch (merch) — daughter, girl; noun f., softened after a woman's name (Riannon uerch Heueyd 'Rhiannon daughter of Hefeydd') · also soft after predicative yn (yn uerch y urenhin 'as daughter to the king')
o: o (o) — (1) 'of, from' preposition; (2) 'if' before a verb (o gwneuthum gam 'if I did wrong') · also 'on, by' (o pedestric 'on foot'), 'out of, from' (o'th garyat ti 'from love of you'), 'of' a kind (pryt … o uorwyn 'the looks of (any) maiden') · also agent after a verbal noun, 'by' (troi o Pwyll y got 'Pwyll turning the bag'); o gosp 'of punishment'
aruon: Proper name — Arfon, the cantref across the Menai Strait from Môn; no mutation (vowel after yn 'in')
teccaf: tec (teg) — fair, pretty; superlative 'fairest' (yr ardurn teccaf a welsei neb)
r: 'r — the article yr contracted after a vowel, apostrophe half of a'r, y'r, o'r etc.: 'the'
yno: yno (yno) — there; adverb (ac yno y bu y nos honno)
ynteu: ynteu (yntau) — 'he, for his part'; conjunctive pronoun marking a change of speaker or actor (heb ynteu)
yg: yn (yn) — in; preposition, spelt yg before a g: the g is the written trace of the nasal mutation (yg gwyd = yng ngwyd 'in the presence of'; yg got = yng nghod 'in a bag', with c>ngh after yn 'in') · also before k-: yg kylch y ty 'around the house' (yng nghylch), the g being the trace of the nasal mutation (c>ngh)
kaer: caer (caer) — fortress, walled town, fort; noun f., first element of the place-name Kaer Seint 'Caer Seint'
yd: yd — preverbal particle used when the clause opens with an adverb rather than the subject, introducing an indicative main verb (A threigylgweith yd oed yn Arberth) · also yd 'corn, grain' noun m. (y diua dy yd 'to destroy your corn')
allei: gallu (gallu) — to be able; 3 sg. imperfect 'he/she could' (hyt na allei dywedut 'so that he could not speak'); g lost by soft mutation after the negative na
wlat: gwlat (gwlad) — land, country; noun f., soft-mutated after the feminine article or possessive (y wlat; i'th wlat) · also soft as the object of a verb, with an adverb between (ny welsynt eiryoet wlat gyuanhedach 'they had never seen a more settled land')
chwaer: chwaer (chwaer) — sister; noun f. (dy chwaer 'your sister'; yn chwaer y minheu 'a sister to me'); no mutation (chw- has no mutated form after dy or yn)
teulu: teulu (teulu) — household-troop, warband, a lord's retinue; noun m. (later came to mean 'family')
wy: wynt (hwynt) — they; 3 pl. pronoun, spelling variant (heb wy 'said they') · also emphatic 'them' after a conjugated preposition (ganthunt wy 'from them', ohonunt wy 'of them') · also 'them' as object, resuming the infixed -s (bei as caffwnn i wy oll 'if I were to get them all') · also a spelling of uy 'my' (wy gwreic i 'my wife'; the nasal mutation is not written)
drostaw: tros (tros) — for, on behalf of; conjugated preposition 'for him' (3 sg. m.) (drostaw 'on his behalf')
wastat: gwastat (gwastad) — constant, level; adjective, soft-mutated after yn (yn ryuelu arnaf yn wastat 'warring on me constantly')
dodes: dodi (dodi) — to put, place; 3 sg. preterite 'put' (a dodes hut ar y wlat 'who put an enchantment on the land'); after the relative a, where d>dd would be unseen in the spelling
uryt: bryt (bryd) — mind, intent; noun m., soft-mutated after y 'his' (yn y uryt 'into his mind') · also ar uryt 'in the mind of', to the eye of, soft after ar (ar uryt y neb a'y guelei 'to the eye of anyone who saw it') · also soft after 'th 'your' (y'th uryt ti 'in your mind')
hyt: hyt (hyd) — as far as, until; preposition/conjunction (hyt ym penn y ulwydyn 'until the year's end'; hyt na bo 'so that there be not') · also ar hyt 'along' (ar hyt y prifford 'along the highway') · also 'as far as, so far as, as much as, to the extent that' with the subjunctive (hyt y mynnych 'as much as you wish'; hyt y gallwyf y gaffael 'as far as I can get it'); hyt oet y wled 'until the time of the feast' · also 'so that' with the indicative (hyt nat oed rym 'so that there was no use'); hyt yn Aberfraw 'as far as Aberffraw' · also the noun 'length, duration' after pa 'what' (Pa hyt bynnac y bydynt ar y ford 'however long they were on the road')
na: na — (1) negative particle in a subordinate clause, 'not' (na dywedy di); (2) 'neither/nor' in a series (na guas ystauell, na swydawc) · also negative imperative 'do not', with soft mutation (na ouyn di 'do not ask'; na yrrwch geu arnaf 'do not lay a lie on me'; na hawl ef 'do not claim him') · also 'not' in a main-clause denial or refusal, with soft mutation (na ellynghaf 'I will not release'; na uynhaf 'I will not have it'; na weleis 'I have not seen')
wydat: gwybot (gwybod) — to know; 3 sg. imperfect 'he knew' (na wydat pwy a'e lladei 'that he did not know who was killing them'; the Red Book wydyat); g- lost by soft mutation after na · also soft after the negative ny (Ac ny wydat 'and he did not know')
beth: beth — what; interrogative pronoun (beth amgen 'what else?', beth a wnaf 'what shall I do?')
nachaf: nachaf (no modern form) — behold, lo; presentative particle that sets the scene before the eyes (nachaf un o'r llongeu 'behold one of the ships'); no mutation
liw: lliw (lliw) — colour; noun m., soft-mutated as object (ar liw yr erchwys)
wed: gwedd (gwedd) — manner, fashion, way; noun f.; g lost by soft mutation after the feminine article y (ar y wed y guelsei 'in the manner that he had seen')
ansawd: ansawd — (1) form, appearance (pryt ac ansawd 'form and appearance'); (2) means, condition (Nit oes ansawd y mi 'I have no means')
charyat: karyat (cariad) — love; noun m., spirant-mutated after a (a charyat arnei 'and love for her')
nat: na, nat (nad) — 'that … not'; negative conjunction of a subordinate clause, nat before a vowel (nat a odyno 'that he does not go from there')
hawd: hawd (hawdd) — easy; adjective (nat hawd genhyf i 'it is not easy with me'); no mutation (h-)
adnabot: adnabot (adnabod) — to know, recognise; verbal noun (adnabot meithryn yr ederyn 'recognising the nursing of the bird')
wnaeth: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 3 sg. preterite 'he did', soft-mutated after a; auxiliary in 'verbal noun + a wnaeth' (dechreu ymdidan a wnaeth)
dydgweith: dydgweith (no modern form) — one day, on a day; dyd 'day' + gweith 'time', adverbial (yn dadleu idaw dydgweith 'debating one day')
arnaw: ar — conjugated preposition 'on him, on it' (llithiau dy erchwys dy hun arnaw 'feeding your own pack on it')
graf: craf (craff) — keen, sharp, intent; adjective, spelt graf (edrych ar y mab yn graf 'to look intently at the boy'); soft-mutated (c>g) after predicative yn · also craf (craff) 'grip, hold', noun m. (ny caei graf 'he could get no grip'); soft-mutated (c>g) as object of a negative verb
was: gwas (gwas) — lad, servant; noun m., soft-mutated in address (Ha was 'ho, lad'; Bid parawt … was 'be ready, lad') and after wrth (wrth was y uarch 'to his groom', literally 'the lad of his horse') · also soft after predicative yn (yn was ieuanc 'as a young lad')
heb: heb — (1) 'said' (heb ef 'said he'), a defective verb used only for tagging speech; (2) 'without' + verbal noun (heb hanbwyllaw 'without troubling') · (3) 'past, beside' in heb law (heb law yr orssed 'past the mound'); see hebdaw · also 'without' + noun (heb ohir 'without delay')
pa: pa (pa) — what, which; interrogative adjective, triggers soft mutation of the following noun
deryw: daruot (darfod) — to end, be over, come to pass; 3 sg. present with perfect sense, 'has ended, is over' (Ar ny deryw o'r wled 'what is not finished of the feast'); softened after ny, but d also writes dd, so the change does not show
ytti: y (i) + ti — 'to you'; conjugated preposition, 2 sg., spelt ytti (y dalu ytti 'to repay it to you'); no mutation
wely: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 2 sg. present 'you will see', soft-mutated after a (ti a wely a wneuthum i yrot ti) · also in the presentative (a) wely di 'do you see?' = 'behold' (Ac wely dy yna dy uab 'and there, behold, is your son'; the Red Book has weldy), softened after the question particle a, which is absorbed
di: di — 'you' (sg.), echoing pronoun after a verb or possessive (y pryny di; dy gerennyd di); also the object 'you' (ni ladaf i di)
arnaf: ar — conjugated preposition 'on me' (arnaf i 'on me')
i: i — (1) emphatic independent pronoun 'I/me', echoing a verb or conjugated preposition (rof i, arnaf i); (2) spelling of y 'to' before a vowel or l/w (i waret); (3) spelling of y 'his' before some words (i wisc hela 'his hunting-dress') · (4) after ohonawch, probably the 2 pl. echoing pronoun chwi with its ch run into the ending (ohonawch i 'of you') · also echoing a possessive (wy gwreic i yw hi 'she is my wife')
arnat: ar — conjugated preposition 'on you' (sg.) (y mae arnat o anryded 'there is rank on you'; a'm ansawd arnat ti)
colli: colli (colli) — to lose; verbal noun (wedy eu colli 'lost', lit. 'after their losing'; yn colli 'losing'); radical after eu and after the yn of the progressive
dy: dy — 'your' (sg.); possessive pronoun, causes soft mutation (dy gerennyd 'your friendship') · also written for the affixed pronoun di 'you' after the presentative wely (Ac wely dy yna dy uab 'and there, behold, is your son')
bryt: bryt (bryd) — mind, intent, purpose, mood; noun m., t for d (ac y bryt ar eu dienydyaw 'and their mind on putting them to death', the y being eu 'their'); radical
th: 'th — infixed/proclitic pronoun, apostrophe half of a'th, i'th, dy'th etc.: 'your' (possessive) or 'you' (object)
pha: pa (pa) — what, which; interrogative, spirant-mutated after a 'and' (a pha wlat 'and what land')
yti: y (i) + ti — conjugated preposition 'to you', variant spelling (pa furyf y caf i dy gerennyd di... yti)
urawt: brawt (brawd) — brother; noun m.; soft-mutated (b>u) after the possessive y 'his' (Manawydan uab Llyr y urawt 'Manawydan son of Llŷr his brother')
hynn: hynn (hyn) — 'this'; demonstrative, substantive use in ual hynn 'like this, thus' · also adjective 'this' after its noun (seith cantref hynn 'these seven cantrefs')
ymi: y (i) + mi — conjugated preposition 'to me' (pa gyuarwyd a uyd ymi)
neb: neb (neb) — anyone; pronoun, used with a positive sense in relative/superlative clauses (o'r a welsei neb 'that anyone had seen') · also 'anyone' under a negative = 'no one' (ny thykya y neb ymlit 'it avails no one to pursue') · also in y neb a 'the one who/to whom' (y neb a dylyer y kymryt y ganthaw 'the one from whom one ought to take it')
yw: bot (bod) — to be; present 3 sg. copula 'is', used in equative sentences (Sef yw hwnnw, Hafgan)
eneit: eneit (enaid) — soul; used in address as an endearment 'dear one, my soul' (a dos y eisted, eneit 'and go to sit, friend')
wdost: gwybot (gwybod) — to know; 2 sg. present 'you know' (ti a wdost 'you know'); soft-mutated (g lost) after the particle a
ba: pa (pa) — what, which; interrogative, a variant spelling with b (Ba ryw leidyr 'what kind of thief'; cf. byhyt for py hyt); whether b is a mutation here is uncertain; causes soft mutation of a following noun
bynnac: bynnac (bynnag) — -ever, indefinite particle after peth/pwy etc.; 'Peth bynnac' 'whatever'
uychanet: bychan (bychan) — small, little; equative bychanet 'as small, how small', here used as a noun of degree, 'the smallness' (uychanet a gawssei o iawn 'how small was what he had got of compensation'); written soft-mutated (b>u)
uo: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may be', soft-mutated after phan 'when' (phan uo ef ar perued 'when he is in the middle of') · also soft-mutated after the relative a (llathen aryant a uo kyuref 'a rod of silver that may be as thick')
rwng: rwng (rhwng) — between; preposition, base uninflected form
dynnyon: dyn (dyn) — person; noun m., plural dynnyon (modern dynion) 'people' (Mab y dynnyon mwyn yw 'he is a son of gentle folk', y 'to'); the softening of d (dd) after y 'to' is not shown
ry: ry — perfective verbal particle 'has, had' before a verb; causes soft mutation (ry adoed 'had gone')
ie: ie — yes; particle of assent, taking up what was just said
taw: tewi (tewi) — to be silent; 2 sg. imperative 'be silent!, hush' (Taw, hyt y mynnych 'be quiet, as much as you like'); modern taw
bellach: bellach — any longer, henceforth; adverb (y'ch kynnal chwi bellach 'to maintain you any longer')
mi: mi — 1 sg. independent/emphatic pronoun 'I' (mi a wnn 'I know')
wnn: gwybot (gwybod) — to know; 1 sg. present 'I know', soft-mutated after a/ny, g dropped (mi a wnn; ny wnn i)
uedwl: medwl (meddwl) — mind, thought; noun m., soft-mutated after y 'his' (yn y uedwl) · also soft-mutated (m>u) after pa 'what' (pa uedwl yw yr eidunt 'what intention is theirs') · also soft-mutated (m>u, = f) after ar 'on' (ar uedwl medi 'on the thought of reaping')
wyt: bot (bod) — to be; 2 sg. present 'you are' (pwy wyt ti 'who are you')
yna: yna (yna) — then; adverb (Yna y rodes Arawn y furuf)
pan: pan (pan) — when; temporal conjunction with a past-time clause (pan doeth) · also interrogative 'from where, whence' (pan doy di? 'where do you come from?') · also 'from where' as a relative (Pan doaf o Loygyr 'from where I come, from England')
wybu: gwybot (gwybod) — to know, perceive; 3 sg. preterite 'knew', soft-mutated after pan 'when' (a phan wybu ef 'and when he knew')
dodi: dodi (dodi) — to put; verbal noun (dodi y deudroet yn y got 'to put his two feet in the bag'; dodi llef ar y gorn 'to give a blast on the horn')
ucheneit: ucheneit (ochenaid) — sigh, groan; noun f.; object of the verbal noun dodi, no mutation (vowel); the adjective follows softened (ucheneit uawr 'a great sigh')
byt: byt (byd) — world; noun m. (o helgwn y byt 'of the hunting dogs of the world')
nyt: ny (nid) — negative particle 'not, it is not', spelling before a vowel or in emphasis (nyt teilygdawt)
minheu: minheu (minnau) — I for my part; conjunctive 1 sg. pronoun, beside innheu (Minheu a baraf 'and I for my part will cause')
baraf: peri (peri) — to cause, bring about; 1 sg. present 'I will cause', soft-mutated after a (Mi a baraf)
cany: cany — 'since … not'; conjunction can 'since' + the negative ny, softening the verb (Cany welas ef 'since he did not see') · also with the verb left unsoftened (Cany mynny hynny 'since you do not want that'; the Red Book likewise)
ellir: gallu (gallu) — to be able; impersonal present 'one can' (Peth a ellir wrth hynny? 'what can be done about that?'), -ir, a>e by affection; soft-mutated (g>∅) after the relative a
geissaw: keissaw (ceisio) — to seek, try; verbal noun in -aw (ar geissaw eu llad 'on seeking to kill them'); soft-mutated (c>g) after ar 'on'
byd: bot (bod) — to be; used two ways: 3 sg. future 'will be' (uyd elsewhere) and, with y-, the vivid present ual y byd 'as he is' · also 2 sg. imperative 'be!' (byd ditheu a'r got honn genhyt 'you be there with this bag') · also byt 'world', spelt with d (eliwlu y byd o lygot 'the world's host of mice'; the Red Book y byt)
yt: y 'to' — conjugated preposition, 2 sg. 'to you', modern iti, spelt yt beside itt and itti (Duw a ro da yt 'may God give you good'; rac anglot yt 'for fear of dishonour to you'; ef a ouyn yt 'he will ask you'; derw yt 'it has befallen you') · also yt (ŷd) 'corn, grain', noun m. (yr yt arall 'the other corn')
at: at — preposition 'to, towards' (at y cwn 'to the dogs')
aethant: mynet (mynd) — to go; 3 pl. preterite 'they went' (yd aethant 'they went')
gigleu: klywet (clywed) — to hear; old 3 sg. preterite 'heard' (a diskyr a gigleu 'and a scream he heard'; yny gigleu 'until he heard'); soft-mutated (k>g) after the relative a or after yny
dyuot: dyuot (dyfod) — to come; verbal noun (a dyuot y Lynn Cuch 'and coming to Glyn Cuch')
ryw: ryw (rhyw) — some, some kind of; before its noun (ryw ystyr hut 'some meaning of magic') · also y ryw wr 'what kind of man'; ryw 'sort, kind' as a noun
ni: ni — (1) 1 pl. pronoun 'we/us' (yd ymdidanyssam ni); (2) negative particle, spelling variant of ny before some verbs (ni ladaf, ni bu)
doeth: dyuot (dod) — to come; 3 sg. preterite 'came' (a doeth 'and came')
ynys: ynys (ynys) — island; noun f. (yr ynys hon 'this island'); no mutation
honn: hon (hon) — 'this' (f.); variant spelling of hon (no'r ulwydyn honn 'than this year')
eiroet: eiroet (erioed) — ever, always (of the past); adverb (a welsei eiroet 'that he had ever seen')
pwy: pwy (pwy) — who; interrogative pronoun (pwy wyt ti 'who are you')
guell: guell (gwell) — better; comparative adjective, in kyuarch guell 'greet' (literally 'ask better')
kic: kic (cig) — meat, flesh; noun m. (-c = g); object of the verbal noun, no mutation
no: no (na) — than, comparative particle (no gyrru 'than driving'; no chyuedach) · also in kyn no hynny 'before that, earlier than that'
wynteu: wynt (hwynt) — they, for their part; conjunctive 3 pl. pronoun (Wynteu hagen ni wybuyssynt)
maent: bot (bod) — to be; 3 pl. present 'they are' (y maent yn lluossauc 'they are numerous'); no mutation
moch: moch (moch) — pigs; collective plural of mochyn 'pig' (eu moch 'their pigs'); no mutation
gelwir: galw (galw) — to call, name; impersonal present 'is called' (Ac y gelwir y rei hynny 'and those are called'), -ir, a>e by affection; no mutation after the particle y
weithon: weithon (weithian) — now, at last; adverb, always in this softened form (gweith 'time' + hon 'this'); par weithon wahard 'have (them) forbidden now'
idaw: idaw (iddo) — to him; 3 sg. m. conjugated form of y 'to'
annwn: Annwn — Annwfn, the realm of Arawn; proper name, in Penn Annwn 'Head of Annwfn' (Pwyll ynteu Penn Annwn); spelt Annwn here, Annwuyn in the first part (and in the Red Book here)
gan: gan (gan) — with, by; preposition, softening the next word; possession is 'with' a person or thing (oed gan y march 'the horse had', literally 'was with the horse'); y gan 'from' (y gan y uarch 'from his horse'); base of gennyf, ganthaw, genthi etc. · also 'from', without y (ny chaffei namyn yr un atteb gan y gwraged 'she would get only the same answer from the women'; yny gigleu gan lawer 'until he heard from many')
arawn: Arawn — proper name, king of Annwfn; meaning unknown
urenhin: brenhin (brenin) — king; noun m., soft-mutated (in apposition or as object): Hafgan urenhin, y deu urenhin · also soft as the predicate complement (a oed urenhin coronawc 'was a crowned king')
etwa: etwa (eto) — yet, still; adverb (nys mynnaf etwa 'I do not want him yet')
ys: ys (ys) — 'it is'; copula particle introducing a predicate, esp. in time expressions (ys blwydyn 'it is a year' = for a year) · also the infixed 3 sg. object 's 'it' after pei (pei ys guelwn 'if I saw it') · also 'below, under', is, in the name Wynt Ys Coet 'Gwent Is Coed' · also before the verb in ac aduyd ys kymeraf 'and perhaps I will take' (the Red Book atuyd ys kymeraf): perhaps the particle, perhaps the infixed 's 'it' after aduyd; uncertain
enw: enw (enw) — name; noun m. (y enw ef 'his name')
hwnnw: hwnnw (hwnnw) — 'that' (m.); demonstrative (y dyd hwnnw 'that day') · also pronoun 'that one' (A hwnnw uu y trydyd dyn 'and that one was the third man'; yw hwnnw 'that is it')
hanner: hanner (hanner) — half; noun m. (yn deu hanner 'into two halves')
furuf: ffuryf (ffurf) — form, shape; noun f.; ff does not mutate, the single f is the scribe's spelling (y furuf 'his form')
gantaw: gan (gan) — 'with him'; conjugated preposition, 3 sg. m., spelt gantaw (hyspys oed gantaw 'it was known to him'); no mutation
af: mynet (mynd) — to go; 1 sg. present/future 'I go, I will go' (a af 'will go')
uyn: mynnu (mynnu) — to wish, want; 3 sg. present 'wants' (A uyn ef dyuot y'r tir 'does he want to come ashore?'); soft-mutated (m>u) after the interrogative particle a · also uy (fy) 'my', with the nasal mutation of d- written as n on the possessive (uyn diua i 'my destruction') · also before teulu (uyn teulu 'my warband'), the n of the nasal mutation being written on the possessive
rith: rith (rhith) — shape, form, guise; noun m. (byd di i'm rith yno 'be there in my shape')
erchi: erchi (erchi) — to ask, request, bid; verbal noun (y erchi it 'to ask of you')
eill: gallu (gallu) — to be able; 3 sg. present, irregular form 'may, can' (ef a eill uot 'it may be')
ych: ych (eich) — your (pl.); possessive pronoun (kymerwch ych kyuarwyd)
nit: nyt (nid) — negative particle 'not, there is not', spelling before a vowel (Nit oes; Nit yttoydwn)
drwc: drwc (drwg) — evil, harm, wrong; noun m. (ny chewch un drwc 'you will get no harm'); no mutation · also the adjective 'bad', as a fronted predicate (ys drwc a gedymdeith uuosti 'a bad companion you were')
doaf: dyuot (dod) — to come; 1 sg. present 'I come' (Pan doaf o Loygyr 'from where I come, from England'); no mutation
en: yn (yn) — in; preposition, spelt en (En Iwerdon 'in Ireland'); no mutation (vowel)
llawen: llawen (llawen) — glad, gladly; adjective, base form (yn llawen)
ragot: rac (rhag) + ti — conjugated preposition 'before you' (ny russya dim ragot)
aeth: mynet (mynd) — to go; 3 sg. preterite 'went' (a'y vreic a aeth attaw 'and his wife went to him')
wynt: wynt (hwynt) — they, them; 3 pl. pronoun (un lliw ac wynt 'the same colour as them') · also Wynt, Gwent, in the name Wynt Ys Coet 'Gwent Is Coed', a region of south-east Wales
lle: lle (lle) — place; noun m., base unmutated form
llys: llys (llys) — court; noun f., base form
doethant: dyuot (dod) — to come; 3 pl. preterite 'they came' (Y'r llys y doethant 'to the court they came')
ymywn: y mywn (mewn) — in, inside; preposition, the old y + mywn (ymywn ty 'inside a house'); no mutation
uuant: bot (bod) — to be; 3 pl. preterite 'they were' (buant); soft-mutated (b>u) after ban 'until, when' (hyt ban uuant weisson mawr 'until they were big lads')
wrthunt: wrth (wrth) + wynt — 'to, at, towards them'; conjugated preposition, 3 pl. (a uu wrthunt 'there was to them'); no mutation
nos: nos (nos) — night; noun f. (y nos honno 'that night')
da: da — good; adjective, also 'goods, wealth' as a noun (treulaw dy da 'spending your wealth')
genhym: gan (gan) — with; conjugated preposition 1 pl. 'with us' (mae genhym ni chwedleu 'we have tidings')
kyuarwydyt: kyuarwydyt (cyfarwyddyd) — tale, story, storytelling (the old sense; the modern word means 'guidance'); noun m. (y kyuarwydyt hwnnw 'that tale'); radical after the article
racco: racco (acw) — yonder; adverb after a noun (yr unbennes racco 'the lady yonder')
moes: moes — give (me)!; an old imperative found only in this form (Moes uy march 'give me my horse')
gyntaf: kyntaf (cyntaf) — first; superlative, soft-mutated after y (ar y gossot kyntaf 'at the first onset') · also adverbial 'fastest, soonest' (ual y gallei gyntaf 'as fast as he could')
wr: gwr (gŵr) — man; noun m., soft-mutated as object (ansyberwyt uwy ar wr) · also soft after y 'to' (y wr 'to a man, to a husband') · also soft in address (A wr 'O man') and after ryw 'kind of' (pa ryw wr 'what kind of man') · also subject directly after a negated verb, soft-mutated (Ny doey wr mawr 'no great man would come')
mawr: mawr (mawr) — big, great; adjective (uarch erchlas mawr 'a big dapple-grey horse')
dywedut: dywedut (dweud) — to say, speak; verbal noun/infinitive
dywedaf: dywedut (dweud) — to say, speak; 1 sg. present 'I say' (Dywedaf wrthyt 'I say to you')
goreu: goreu (gorau) — best; superlative of da 'good' (Goreu yw gennyf 'it is best with me' = I prefer)
kyuarwyd: kyuarwyd (cyfarwydd) — guidance, direction, information; noun m. (pa gyuarwyd a uyd ymi)
digrif: digrif (digri) — pleasant, amusing; adjective (y bu digrif ganthaw 'it was pleasant to him')
yny: yny (hyd oni) — until; so that; conjunction, with a vivid present (yny hyllt, yny dyrr, yny uyd) or the subjunctive for a future goal (yny delych) · also in Ac ar yny llyma, a slip for ar hynny 'thereupon', kept as written (the Red Book has ar hynny) (Ac ar yny, llyma y teulu 'and thereupon, behold the warband')
hoff: hoff (hoff) — dear, pleasing, beloved; adjective, predicate (nyt hoff honno 'that (craft) is not pleasing'); no mutation
paub: pawb (pawb) — everyone; pronoun, spelt paub with u for w (yd eistedwys paub 'everyone sat')
ymdidan: ymdidan (ymddiddan) — conversation, to converse; noun/verbal noun, base form (dechreu ymdidan a wnaeth ef)
diwed: diwed (diwedd) — end, close; noun m., d spells dd; radical after the article y (yn y diwed 'in the end')
ae: ae (ae) — either … or; correlative conjunction (ae a'e droet ae a throssawl 'either with his foot or with a staff'); no mutation
gwna: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 2 sg. imperative 'make!, do!' (gwna oed a mi 'make an appointment with me')
uy: uy (fy) — my; possessive pronoun, triggers nasal mutation (uy anryded; uy nghyffes; uy gherennyd)
neges: neges (neges) — errand, business; noun f. (yd oed neges idi 'she had an errand'; Pennaf neges 'the chief errand')
wrthyt: wrth (wrth) + ti — conjugated preposition 'to/at you' (Dywedaf wrthyt; chadw kywirdeb wrthyt titheu)
uu: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. preterite 'was' (bu), soft-mutated after a (tirionwch... a uu y ryngthunt) · also soft-mutated after tra 'while' (tra uu da ganthunt 'while it was good with them') · also soft-mutated after yny 'until' (yny uu damunet gantunt 'until there was desire in them') and as after the relative a left unwritten (A hwnnw uu y trydyd dyn 'and that one was the third man') · also 'she was' after a fronted predicate, the relative a understood (a lleidyr uu hi arnaf i 'and a thief she was against me')
hun: hun (hun) — self, own; also 'sleep' as a separate noun by context (e hunan/e hun 'himself'; kymryt hun 'to take sleep')
well: gwell (gwell) — better; comparative of da 'good', soft-mutated as the object of kyuarch (ny chyuarchaf i well it 'I do not greet you') · also soft as a comparative standing after its noun (seith cantref well 'seven better cantrefs'; heldir well 'a better hunting-land') · also soft as the predicate straight after the verb (nat oed well genti 'it was no better to her')
llyna: llyna (dyna) — there is, behold that; presentative particle, distal counterpart of llyma
inheu: inheu (innau) — I/mine, for my part; conjunctive 1 sg. pronoun marking contrast (a'm kyuoeth inheu 'my realm, mine')
thidi: ti + di (tydi) — you; 2 sg. pronoun with the affixed di, 'you yourself' (a thidi 'with you'); spirant-mutated (t>th) after a 'with, as' (kyuurd a thidi 'as equal in rank as you')
am: am — preposition 'about, around; concerning' (am y uynwgyl 'about his neck'; am dir a dayar 'about land') · also 'for, in return for' (am y gam 'for his wrong'; am pob un 'for each one')
it: itt (iti) — to you; 2 sg. conjugated preposition, spelling variant with single t (achos it heuyt)
annwuyn: Annwuyn (Annwfn, Annwn) — the realm Arawn rules, a world alongside this one; proper name
hawssaf: hawd (hawdd) — easy; superlative hawssaf 'easiest' (-af, modern hawsaf); adjective, as predicate (hawssaf yw in ymborth yno 'it is easiest for us to get food there'); no mutation
by: pa (pa) — what, which; spelt by (by ryw neges 'what kind of errand'); causes soft mutation of the following word (ryw from rhyw)
bei: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. imperfect subjunctive 'were, would be' (bei ar y gam 'if it were at its step' = at a walk) · also the conjunction 'if' (bei ymladem ni ac wyntwy 'if we fought with them')
ammot: ammot (amod) — agreement, terms, condition; noun m. (llunnya dy ammot 'devise your terms'; yr ammot hwnnw 'that agreement')
rof: rwng (rhwng) + i — conjugated preposition 'between me' (y rof i a Duw 'between me and God')
m: 'm — infixed/proclitic pronoun, apostrophe half of a'm, y'm, o'm etc.: 'my' (possessive, triggers soft mutation) or 'me' (object) · with h- before a following vowel (o'm hanwod 'against my will'); as 'my' before a verbal noun it may stand for that noun's object (a'm rodi 'and my giving' = and giving me); as 'me' after a relative (a'm gwrthyt 'who rejects me')
gwlat: gwlat (gwlad) — land, country; noun f. (ar gynghor uy gwlat 'to the counsel of my country'); no mutation shown after uy 'my' (the nasal mutation, ngwlat, is not written)
amdanunt: am (am) + wynt — 'about them'; conjugated preposition, 3 pl. (wiscaw amdanunt 'to dress about them'); no mutation
genhyf: gan (gan) — with, conjugated 1 sg. 'with me' (eres genhyf 'strange with me'; ryued oed genhyf 'it was a wonder with me'); the gan 'with' of opinion; no mutation
deu: deu (dau) — two (m.); numeral, causes soft mutation of a following noun (y deu wrenhin 'the two kings')
kymeint: kymeint (cymaint) — as much, so much, as great; noun/pronoun, kymeint ac 'as much as' (Kymeint ac a ercheist 'as much as you asked')
allaf: gallu (gallu) — to be able; 1 sg. present 'I can', with g lost by soft mutation after ny (Ny allaf ui … 'I cannot')
rydhau: rydhau (rhyddhau) — to free, release; verbal noun (rydhau Riannon a Phryderi 'freeing Rhiannon and Pryderi'); radical
ditheu: ditheu (dithau) — conjunctive form of ti 'you' (sg.), 'you for your part'
ual: ual (fel) — as, like; conjunction/preposition (ual hynn 'like this') · also 'so that' (ual yd ymglywynt 'so that they could hear one another'; ual y bydynt gadarnach 'so that they would be stronger') and 'how' (sef ual yd eistedyssant 'that is how they sat')
dyro: rodi (rhoi) — to give; negative imperative 'do not give!' (na dyro 'do not give') · also the positive imperative 'give!' (dyro ui idaw 'give me to him', Dyro di ui idaw ef 'you give me to him')
im: im (i mi) — to me; conjugated preposition, contracted spelling (Meuyl im 'shame to me')
ui: ui (fi) — me; object pronoun after an imperative (dygwch ui odyma 'carry me from here') · also the softened pronoun 'I' after a verb (Ny allaf ui arnaf a dywedy di uyth 'I cannot bring myself to do what you say') and as the second, emphatic pronoun in mi ui 'I myself' (A mi ui a rodaf 'and I myself will give'); soft-mutated from mi · also after gwae 'woe' (guae ui 'woe is me')
ohonunt: o (o) + wynt — 'of them, from them'; conjugated preposition, 3 pl. (kyscu a wnaeth pawb ohonunt 'every one of them slept'); no mutation
auory: auory (yfory) — tomorrow; adverb (o'r dyd auory 'from the day tomorrow')
gyfnewit: kyfnewit (cyfnewid) — exchange, change; noun m., the last word of the epithet Llassar Llaes Gyfnewit; soft-mutated (k>g) after the preceding adjective llaes
aethont: mynet (mynd) — to go; 3 pl. preterite 'they went', beside aethant (y'r bordeu yd aethont 'to the tables they went')
gedymdeithon: kedymdeith (cydymaith) — companion; plural -on, soft-mutated after possessive y 'his' (a'y gedymdeithon 'and his companions') · also soft as the complement after a verb (A bydwch gedymdeithon chwitheu 'and be companions, you also')
kynghor: kynghor (cyngor) — counsel, advice; noun m., base form (Kynghor yw hynny 'that is counsel'; gan gynghor 'by the counsel')
wyr: gwyr (gwŷr) — men; noun pl., soft-mutated after yn (yn wyr ymi 'as men to me') · also soft after o 'of' (o wyr 'of men') and in address (A wyr 'O men') · also soft after y 'to' (y wyr Dyuet 'to the men of Dyfed') and y 'his' (y wyr 'his men')
oc: o (o) — 'of, from', spelt oc before a vowel (oc eu hanuod 'against their will'); no mutation
herchi: erchi (erchi) — to ask; verbal noun, with h-prefix after y 'her' (y herchi hi 'to ask her')
wynte: wynteu (hwythau) — they for their part; conjunctive pronoun 3 pl., spelt wynte without -u (ganthunt wynte 'with them, for their part'); no mutation
cael: caffael (cael) — to get, suffer, receive; verbal noun, cael beside caffael (ouyn cael kymriw 'fear of getting injury')
dangos: dangos (dangos) — to show, make known; verbal noun (y erchi … dangos 'to bid (them) show themselves')
hut: hut (hud) — magic, illusion, enchantment; noun m. (ystyr hut 'a meaning of magic')
du: dy (dy) — your; 2 sg. possessive, written du here, a slip for dy (Evans prints du; the Red Book has dy hun) (du hun 'yourself'); causes soft mutation (none visible before h-)
pob: pob (pob) — each, every; adjective (pob un 'each one')
honunt: o — conjugated preposition 'of/from them', truncated (o honunt 'of them')
arnunt: ar — conjugated preposition 'on them' (Sef lliw oed arnunt 'this was the colour that was on them')
guelei: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 3 sg. imperfect, soft-mutated after y (Llyma y guelei ef 'there he saw')
bydynt: bot (bod) — to be; 3 pl. habitual imperfect 'they were (being), they used to be', beside oedynt (ual y bydynt yn eisted 'as they were sitting')
meirch: march (march) — horse; noun pl. (meirch a milgwn 'horses and greyhounds')
dylyei: dylyu (dylu) — to owe, deserve; 3 sg. imperfect, negated 'would not deserve' (ual nas dylyei 'such that it would not deserve it') · also positive 'ought' (y rann a dylyei uot am y hwyneb 'the part that ought to be about her face')
hayarn: haearn (haearn) — iron; noun m., spelt hayarn (y ty hayarn 'the iron house'); no mutation (apposed after the noun ty)
uot: bot (bod) — to be; verbal noun, soft-mutated after a (ef a eill uot yn ediuar gennyf) · also soft as the complement of a verb (a dylyei uot 'that ought to be') · also soft-mutated after y 'his' (y uot yn colli 'that he was losing', lit. 'his being losing') · also soft after dy 'your' (dy uot yn kyuanhedu 'your being settled')
gwbyl: cwbyl (cwbl) — whole, complete; adjective; soft-mutated (c>g) as the predicate after uu (yny uu gwbyl idaw y dal 'until his payment was complete to him') · also soft-mutated (c>g) as object after ry geueist (neu ry geueist gwbyl 'you have got the whole')
weith: gwaith (gwaith) — work, make, pattern, manner; noun m. (MW gweith); g lost by soft mutation after ar (ar weith taryaneu da 'after the pattern of good shields, on the work of good shields'); the sense 'manner, pattern' is a little uncertain · also soft-mutated (gw>w) as the object of welsynt (y lle ny welsynt eiryoet weith 'where they had never seen work'); gweith 'time' is possible but less likely · also soft after ryw 'kind of' (pa ryw weith 'what kind of work') and after y (gohir ar y weith 'delay over the work')
cwn: ci (ci) — dogs; noun pl. of ci, the pack as individual animals (as against erchwys, the pack as a body)
dyd: dyd (dydd) — day; noun m. (y dyd 'the day'; dyd da 'good day')
ro: rodi (rhoi) — to give; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may he give', in a wish after the particle a; r- shows no mutation (Duw a ro da yt 'may God give you good')
llyma: llyma (dyma) — behold, here is; presentative particle throwing a scene before the reader (llyma yr erchwys)
geir: geir (gair) — word; noun m.; geir is the Middle Welsh spelling, no mutation after un with a masculine noun (un geir 'one word') · also 'near, by', a spelling of ger (ymauael a'r ebawl geir y uwng 'seizing the foal by its mane')
dywedeist: dywedut (dweud) — to say; 2 sg. preterite 'you said' (y geir a dywedeist 'the word you said'), modern dywedaist
neithwyr: neithwyr (neithiwr) — last night; adverb (yr blwydyn y neithwyr 'a year ago tonight')
nas: ny + 's — negative particle ny with infixed 3 sg. object pronoun 's 'it/him': 'that not it/him' (ual nas dylyei)
titheu: ti (ti) — you, for your part; conjunctive 2 sg. pronoun
elly: gallu (gallu) — to be able; 2 sg. present, soft-mutated/g-dropped after a ('a hynny a elly yn haut' 'and that you can do easily')
rodaf: rodi (rhoi) — to give, put; 1 sg. present/future 'I will give/put' (mi a'th rodaf di)
kyfrwyeu: kyfrwy (cyfrwy) — saddle; noun m., plural in -eu (modern cyfrwyau) (gwneuthur kyfrwyeu 'making saddles'); radical
guely: guely (gwely) — bed; noun m. (yn y guely 'into the bed')
taryan: taryan (tarian) — shield; noun f. (dyrchauael taryan 'raising a shield', swch y taryan 'the point of the shield'); no mutation (radical, object of the verbal noun)
eureit: eureit (euraid) — golden; adjective, from aur 'gold' (gwisc eureit 'a golden garment')
gymerwn: kymryt (cymryd) — to take; 1 pl. present/future 'we take, we will take' (-wn) (a chynghor a gymerwn); soft-mutated (k>g) after the particle a
gynghor: kynghor (cyngor) — counsel, advice, will; noun m., soft-mutated after possessive y 'his' (wrth y gynghor ef 'by his counsel'; gan gynghor 'by the counsel of') · also soft as the object of a verb (mi a wnn gynghor da 'I know good counsel') · also soft after a preceding adjective (yn y kyuyng gynghor 'in the narrow counsel') and as object (ni a gymerwn gynghor 'we will take counsel') · also soft after wrth (Reit oed im wrth gynghor 'I could do with counsel') and after pa (a pha gynghor 'and what counsel')
rodi: rodi (rhoi) — to give, put; verbal noun, base form
e: y — 'his', spelt e before a following consonant or in some spellings: e gwn 'his dogs', e weneb 'his face'; also the preposition 'to' in e uynet 'to go' · also 'her', with h- before a vowel (e hymlit hi 'to pursue her'); the verbal particle y (e deuthum i 'I came'); y of y wrth 'from' (e wrthaw 'from him'); and in e uynyd 'up', e ymdeith 'away' · also the article 'the' (E brenhin, E chwedyl 'the king', 'the news'); 'it' as dummy subject (E doeth im 'it came to me') · also the infixed object 'him' after a (pwy a'e lladei 'who killed him'; a'e guelei 'who saw him') and 'her' with spirant mutation (a'e chladu yno 'and burying her there'); and the y of y gan 'from' (E gan Uanawydan 'from Manawydan') · also in e hun (ehun) 'self, own', unchanged for any person (eu kedymdeithon e hun 'their own companions'; synnyaw e hun 'watching for himself')
chymryt: kymryt (cymryd) — to take, put on; verbal noun, spirant-mutated (k>ch) after a 'and' (a chymryt lloppaneu 'and putting on clouts')
taryaneu: taryan (tarian) — shield; noun f., plural in -eu (modern tariannau) (gwnawn taryaneu 'let us make shields'; gweith taryaneu 'work of shields'); radical
dechreussant: dechreu (dechrau) — to begin; 3 pl. preterite in -ssant 'they began' (A'r gyuedach a dechreussant 'and the carousing they began'); no mutation shown after the relative a (the soft mutation of d- is not written)
gerdet: kerdet (cerdded) — going, pace; verbal noun/noun, soft-mutated after y 'to' (y gerdet 'to go'), after vn 'same' (vn gerdet; why is not clear, kerdet being usually masculine), and in amgen urys gerdet 'other haste of pace' (cause unclear) · also soft-mutated after pa 'what' (pa gerdet yssyd arnawch chwi 'what journey is on you?') and after llyna (Llyna gerdet 'there is the journey') · also soft after ar 'on' (ar gerdet 'on the move, walking')
reit: reit (rhaid) — need, necessity; noun m./f. (reit ymi 'need to me' = 'I need')
in: y (i) + ni — 'to us, for us'; conjugated preposition 1 pl., spelt in (ys guell in 'it is better for us'); no mutation
pryt: pryt (pryd) — form, appearance; noun m. (pryt ac ansawd 'form and appearance')
gilyd: kilid (cilydd) — 'the other, fellow'; variant spelling of gilid (ar y gilyd 'against the other')
kerdyssant: kerdet (cerdded) — to walk, go; 3 pl. preterite in -yssant 'they walked' (Y gyt y kerdyssant 'together they went'); radical after the particle y following the fronted adverb
keredigyawn: Keredigyawn (Ceredigion) — proper name, Ceredigion, the region of west Wales; no mutation
thrannoeth: trannoeth (trannoeth) — the next day; noun/adverb, spirant-mutated after a 'and' (A thrannoeth) · also spirant-mutated after no 'than' (no thrannoeth 'than the next day')
hynt: hynt — way, course, journey; noun f. (dy hynt 'your way')
dros: dros (dros) — over, across; preposition (dros pedrein y uarch 'over the crupper of his horse')
buant: bot (bod) — to be; 3 pl. preterite 'they were' (Ny buant 'they were not')
dref: tref (tref) — town, homestead, settlement; noun f., soft-mutated (t>d) after the feminine article y (ar y dref 'on the town') · also soft after holl (yn yr holl dref 'in the whole town') and after y 'to' (y dref arall 'to another town')
heuyt: heuyt (hefyd) — also, either; adverb (Ni wydwn achos it heuyt 'I did not know a reason for you either')
odyna: odyna (oddi yna, oddyna) — from there, then, after that; adverb, od 'from' + yna 'there' (Odyna treulaw y ulwydyn 'then spending the year')
racdunt: rac (rhag) + wynt — conjugated preposition 3 pl. 'before them' (modern rhagddynt), in -dunt; idiomatic 'on, ahead of them' (a gerdassant racdunt 'walked on their way'), and 'on their account, before them' elsewhere (a lwydwys racdunt 'prospered before them'; dygywys … racdunt 'was galling because of them')
kymwt: kymwt (cwmwd) — commote, a subdivision of a cantref; noun m. (kymwt arall 'another commote'; y kymwt hwnnw 'that commote'); no mutation
ym: yn (yn) — in; preposition, spelling variant before p/m/b (hyt ym Penn Llwyn Diarwya; ym perued) · also bot 1 pl. present 'we are' (yd ym y gyt 'we are together'; llibin yd ym pob blwydyn 'wretched that we are every year') · also 'my', a by-form of uy, in the oath ym kyffes y Duw 'by my confession to God' (the Red Book has ym kyffes i y Duw); the nasal mutation it brings is not written
ystyr: ystyr (ystyr) — meaning, purpose; noun (ryw ystyr hut 'some meaning of magic')
mywn: y mywn (i mewn) — in, inside; adverbial phrase (yn dyuot y mywn 'coming in') · also prepositional 'in' (y mywn gogof 'in a cave')
ha: ha — ho!, ah!; interjection before an address, the noun addressed softened (Ha was 'ho, lad')
ol: ol (ôl) — track, trace; noun m. (yn ol y cwn 'after the hounds'; yn y ol 'in its track')
kyrchyssant: kyrchu (cyrchu) — to go to, make for; 3 pl. preterite in -yssant 'they made for' (y kyrchyssant wynteu Hardlech 'they made for Harlech'; y'r neuad y kyrchyssant 'to the hall they went'); radical after the particle y
uchaf: uchaf (uchaf) — highest, uppermost; superlative of uchel 'high' (yn y lle uchaf 'in the highest place'); follows its noun, radical
gwneuthur: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; verbal noun/infinitive, also used as the periphrastic auxiliary 'do' (a wneuthum itt 'that I did to you')
achaws: achaws (achos) — cause, reason; noun m. ('Pa achaws' 'what reason, why') · also in o achaws 'because of' (o achaws y carchar hwnnw 'because of that prison')
dodet: dodi (dodi) — to put; impersonal 'has been put', after the perfective particle ry (ry dodet ymman 'has been put here') · also impersonal preterite 'was put, was laid' after the relative a (Sef penyt a dodet erni 'this is the penance that was laid on her'; Sef enw a dodet arnaw 'the name that was given him') · also impersonal preterite after the particle y (wrth hynny y dodet ar y kymwt hwnnw 'for that reason it was put on that commote')
guedy: guedy (gwedi) — after; preposition (A guedy y medwl hwnnw 'and after that thought')
phan: pan (pan) — when; spirant-mutated after a 'and' (A phan doeth yno) · also spirant-mutated after no 'than' (no phan uuassei 'than when he had been')
oedit: bot (bod) — to be; impersonal imperfect in -it 'one was, people were' (Ac yn dechreu treulaw y wled yd oedit yn y llys 'and they were beginning to consume the feast in the court'); no mutation
chwedleu: chwedl (chwedl) — tale, story, talk; noun f., plural chwedleu (y chwedleu ereill 'the other tales'); ch- does not mutate here
yssyd: bot (bod) — to be; relative present 'is, who/that is' (sydd) (Gwr yssyd gyuerbyn; pa amgen uedwl yssyd yndaw)
dygyuor: dygyuor (dygyfor) — to muster, rally (a hunt); verbal noun (dechreu dygyuor yr hela 'beginning to muster the hunt') · also noun 'muster, gathering' (Dygyuor y wlat a doeth attunt 'the muster of the land came to them')
mae: bot (bod) — to be; irregular present 3 sg. 'is, there is' (y mae arnat o anryded) · also interrogative 'where is?' (Mae yr yniuer …? 'where is the company …?')
chwi: chwi (chi) — 'you' (pl.); pronoun (y'ch kynnal chwi 'to maintain you')
ryued: ryued (rhyfedd) — wonder, marvel; noun m., also the adjective 'strange' (ryued oed genhyf 'it was a wonder with me'); no mutation
udunt: y (i) + wynt — conjugated preposition 'to them' (Amser a doeth udunt e uynet e gyscu)
arall: arall — other, another; adjective (yr erchwys arall 'the other pack') · also pronoun 'another (woman)' (heb arall 'said another') · also 'again, more' after kymeint (y gymeint arall 'as much again')
wnaethant: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 3 pl. preterite 'they did', soft-mutated after a (eisted a wnaethant)
cherdet: kerdet (cerdded) — to walk, go; verbal noun, spirant-mutated after a (a cherdet yn ol y cwn 'and going after the hounds') · also the noun 'pace, gait', spirant-mutated after y 'her' (y cherdet hitheu 'her pace')
gyscu: kyscu (cysgu) — to sleep; verbal noun, soft-mutated after y (y gyscu 'to sleep')
chymell: kymell (cymell) — to urge, compel, force; verbal noun, spirant-mutated (c>ch) after y 'her' (a'y chymell 'and to force her')
allan: allan — out, forth; adverb ('o hynny allan' 'from then on')
chyscu: kyscu (cysgu) — to sleep; verbal noun; spirant-mutated (k>ch) after a 'and' (a chyscu genthi 'and sleeping with her')
genti: gan (gan) — 'with her'; conjugated preposition, 3 sg. f., spelt genti (a chanawon genti 'and whelps with her'); no mutation
hanuod: anuod (anfodd) — displeasure, unwillingness; noun m., with h-prefix after the contracted 'm 'my' (o'm hanuod 'against my will') · also with h- after eu 'their' (oc eu hanuod 'against their will')
welsant: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 3 pl. preterite 'they saw' (-sant) (pan welsant 'when they saw'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after pan 'when'
drannoeth: trannoeth (trannoeth) — the next day; adverb, the soft-mutated form used adverbially (hanner dyd drannoeth; a mi drannoeth)
kyrchu: kyrchu (cyrchu) — to make for, head towards; verbal noun (Kyrchu y llys a oruc ynteu)
parth: parth (parth) — towards, side, direction; noun m./preposition (parth a'y lys 'towards his court')
lu: llu (llu) — host, army; noun m.; soft-mutated (ll>l) after deu 'two' (y deu lu 'the two hosts') · also soft after 'th 'your' (a'th lu 'and your host')
guyr: gwr (gŵr) — man; plural guyr 'men' (gwŷr); gu- for gw-; no mutation (Y guyr hynny 'those men', after the article)
mynet: mynet (mynd) — to go; verbal noun (amser mynet y uwyta 'time to go to eat')
gymryt: kymryt (cymryd) — to take, receive; verbal noun, soft-mutated after i/y (iawn yw gymryt 'it is right to receive') · also soft-mutated after ar 'on' (disgynnu a wnaeth ar gymryt hynny 'he settled on taking that')
tu: tu (tu) — side, direction; noun m. (y tu ar Gernyw, y tu a Chernyw 'the side towards Cornwall'); no mutation
aros: aros (aros) — to wait, wait for, stay; verbal noun (A'e aros 'and waiting for him', 'e being 'him', the object); no mutation (vowel initial)
dwy: dwy (dwy) — two (f.); numeral, causes soft mutation of a following feminine noun (y dwy dyrnas 'the two kingdoms')
coet: coet (coed) — wood, forest; noun m. (dan y coet 'under the wood')
kyrchwys: kyrchu (cyrchu) — to make for, charge at; 3 sg. preterite 'made for' in -wys (y kyrchwys y bleit 'he charged the wall'); no mutation after the particle y
bu: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. preterite 'was' (a uu 'was'; Llawen uu 'glad was')
gyfranc: kyfranc (cyfranc) — (1) an encounter, a fight; (2) a story, an adventure (its other sense); noun m., soft-mutated after y
llas: lladd (lladd) — to strike, kill, cut off; 3 sg. impersonal/passive preterite 'was struck, was cut' (y llas y benn ef 'his head was struck off'); radical after the particle y
uawr: mawr (mawr) — great, big; adjective (grauanc uawr 'a great claw'); soft-mutated (m>u) after a feminine noun · also predicative, soft-mutated directly after the verb (nyt oed uawr y weilgi 'the sea was not great') · also soft-mutated (m>u, = f) after yn in the adverbial yn uawr 'greatly'
pop: pob (pob) — each, every; adjective, spelling variant (o pop un y gilid)
meint: maint (maint) — size, amount, extent; noun, spelt meint; y meint goruot 'so much victory, the whole measure of victory'; radical
tangneued: tangneued (tangnefedd) — peace; noun f. (ef a barei tangneued 'he would make peace'); no mutation (object, radical)
pedwyryd: pedwerydd (pedwerydd) — fourth; ordinal (pen y pedwyryd ulwydyn 'the end of the fourth year'); no mutation
guyrda: gwyrda (gwŷr da) — noblemen; gwyr 'men' + da 'good', plural noun (A wyrda 'O noblemen')
kerdet: kerdet (cerdded) — going, walking; verbal noun, also a noun 'pace, gait' (kerdet araf guastat 'a slow, even pace'; o'r kerdet mwyaf 'to the greatest pace')
ryd: rhydd (rhydd) — free; adjective (yny uo ryd y wyr 'until his men are free')
ellit: gallu (gallu) — to be able; impersonal imperfect 'could be' (a ellit a'r meirych 'that could be had from the horses'); g- lost by soft mutation after the relative a · also soft after the negative ny (ny ellit 'there could not be')
gyrru: gyrru (gyrru) — to drive; verbal noun (gyrru yr erchwys … e ymdeith 'driving the pack away')
kennadeu: kennat (cennad) — messenger; plural kennadeu 'messengers' (cenhadon); no mutation (subject, radical: Sef kennadeu a aeth 'the messengers who went')
deulu: teulu (teulu) — household-troop, warband; noun m., soft-mutated after 'y (a'y deulu 'and his warband')
gadu: gadu (gadael) — to leave; verbal noun, soft-mutated after eithyr (eithyr gadu 'except to leave')
ryngtaw: rwng (rhwng) + ef — 'between him'; conjugated preposition, 3 sg. m., used in the idiom ryngtaw a 'between him and' = on his way to (Ef a aeth ryngtaw a llys Eueyd Hen 'he went his way to the court of Heueyd the Old')
canys: canys — since, for, because; conjunction (canys dechreueist uy llad 'since you have begun to kill me') · also for kan 'since' + nys 'not … it' (Canys collyghy yr hynny 'since you will not release it for that'; the Red Book Kan nys gellyngy) · also plain affirmative 'since' (A chanys bu 'and since she was')
os: os (os) — if; conjunction of a real condition (os hynny a uynny 'if that is what you want')
uynet: mynet (mynd) — to go; verbal noun, soft-mutated after e/y (e uynet e gyscu 'to go to sleep')
ymlad: ymlad (ymladd) — to fight; verbal noun (yn herwyd ymlad a frouedigaeth y gorff)
wneuthur: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; verbal noun (y wneuthur kynnadeu at Pwyll 'to send envoys to Pwyll', literally 'to make messengers'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after the preposition y 'to' · also soft after y 'its' (yn y wneuthur 'in the making of it'), the possessive standing for the object
ninheu: ni (ni) — we, for our part; conjunctive 1 pl. pronoun (a gaussam ninheu)
gallu: gallu (gallu) — power, ability; noun m. (herwyd uyg gallu i 'according to my power'); nasal-mutated (g>ng) after uy 'my', written uyg gallu with the g on the possessive
dioer: dioer — assuredly, indeed; an oath, a worn-down Duw a wyr 'God knows'
teg: teg (teg) — fair, lovely; adjective after its noun (lle teg brenhineid 'a fair, kingly place'); no mutation
gwr: gwr (gŵr) — man; noun m. (y gwr a oed yn lle Arawn 'the man who was in Arawn's place')
gam: cam (cam) — wrong; noun m., soft-mutated as object (o gwneuthum gam 'if I did wrong') · also cam 'step, pace', noun m., soft after y 'his, its' (bei ar y gam 'if it were at its step' = at a walk) · also soft-mutated after the possessive y 'his' (am y gam 'for his wrong')
erbyn: erbyn (erbyn) — (1) against, by (a time) (erbyn hanner dyd 'by midday'); (2) 'to meet' (yn y erbyn 'to meet him')
eidaw: eiddo (eiddo) — that which belongs to someone, 'his'; the independent possessive in 3 sg. m. (yr eidaw ef 'his'; pa darpar oed yr eidaw 'what purpose was his'); no mutation (vowel)
dygaf: dwyn (dwyn) — to bring, carry; 1 sg. present 'I bring' (y dygaf uy nghyffes 'I bring my confession')
uyg: uy (fy) — my; possessive, here spelt uyg before k-: the g is the written trace of the nasal mutation the noun would take (uyg kyuoeth = fy nghyfoeth 'my realm')
kyffes: kyffes (cyffes) — confession; noun f. (ym kyffes y Duw 'by my confession to God'; the Red Book has ym kyffes i y Duw); ym is taken as 'my', and the nasal mutation it brings (nghyffes) is not shown in the spelling
archaf: erchi (erchi) — to ask; 1 sg. present 'I ask'; the stem vowel is a (arch-), which becomes e in erchi (nyt archaf 'I do not ask'; Sef arch a archaf 'the request I ask')
drossof: tros (tros) — for, on behalf of; conjugated preposition 'for me' (1 sg.) (drossof 'on my behalf')
phryderi: Pryderi (Pryderi) — proper name, Pryderi son of Pwyll and Rhiannon; spirant-mutated (p>ph) after a 'and' (a Phryderi 'and Pryderi')
gouyn: gouyn (gofyn) — to ask; 2 sg. imperative 'ask!' (Gouyn ueithon y Wawl weicheu 'ask Gwawl for sureties') · also verbal noun 'asking', g- lost by soft mutation after heb 'without' (heb ouyn 'without asking') and after y 'to' (y ouyn idaw 'to ask of him'); also in a gouyn a wnaeth 'asking he did'
iawn: iawn — right, proper, correct; adjective/predicate (iawn yw gymryt 'it is right to receive') · also noun 'compensation, redress, amends' (dy iawn 'your compensation'; chael iawn 'getting redress') · also 'right (thing)' as object of gwneuthur (phei gwnelut iawn 'and if you were to do right')
gwyr: gwr (gŵr) — men; noun pl. (kymryt gwrogaeth y gwyr 'taking the homage of the men') · also gwyr 3 sg. present of gwybot 'knows' (onys gwyr Branwen 'unless Branwen knows it')
dechreuwyt: dechreu (dechrau) — to begin; impersonal preterite 'was begun' in -wyt (y dechreuwyt kymyscu y tan 'the mixing of the fire was begun'); no mutation after the particle y
gwiscaw: gwiscaw (gwisgo) — to put on, wear; verbal noun, fronted before a oruc (Gwiscaw bratteu trwm … a oruc Pwyll 'Pwyll put on heavy rags')
nerth: nerth (nerth) — strength, force; noun m. (o nerth cledyueu 'by force of swords')
lledrith: lledrith (lledrith) — illusion, enchantment, shape-changing; noun m. (yr hut a'r lledrith 'the enchantment and the illusion'); radical after the article 'r; also spelt lletrith
maen: maen (maen) — stone; noun m. (na maen na gueith 'neither stone nor work'); radical after na 'neither'
uch: uch (uwch) — above, over; preposition (uch llaw y llys 'above the court') · also 'high' as adjective/adverb, comparative in yn uch no bwrd y llong 'higher than the ship's board'
may: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. present 'is', a spelling of mae, introducing a reported fact (y may brawt un uam a mi a wnaeth hynny 'that it is a brother who did that'); no mutation
gerdassant: kerdet (cerdded) — to walk, travel, go; 3 pl. preterite in -assant 'they travelled' (Wynt a gerdassant trannoeth parth a Dyuet 'they travelled next day towards Dyfed'); soft-mutated (k>g) after the particle a
ganthunt: gan — conjugated preposition 'with them' (ni bu newydach ganthunt 'it was no more novel to them')
harglwyd: arglwyd (arglwydd) — lord; noun m. (a'e harglwyd 'and their lord'); h- prefixed to the vowel after the possessive e/eu 'their'
gollyssynt: colli (colli) — to lose; 3 pl. pluperfect 'they had lost' in -yssynt (collet a gollyssynt 'the loss they had lost'); soft-mutated (c>g) after the relative a
llawer: llawer (llawer) — much, many; noun/adverb (guedy byryer llawer yndi 'after much has been thrown into it')
can: can — hundred; numeral, also 'white' (Hafgan = haf + can 'summer-white'); here in guerth can carw 'the worth of a hundred stags' · also can 'since, because' (can doethwyf i 'since I have come')
mwyaf: mawr (mawr) — big, great; superlative mwyaf 'greatest, most' (o'r kerdet mwyaf 'to the greatest pace')
